text:
Maria G: Heads-up — I opened an RFC follow-up about breaking the runtime monolith into a strangler-style mesh. Wanted to surface tradeoffs before we lock the plan.
Noah T: Nice. Can you TL;DR the approach?
Maria G: TL;DR: incrementally extract hot-path pieces (kv-cache, request-router, session manager) behind lightweight adapters. Proxy traffic to new services gradually via header flags and route rules. Keep one data plane running until feature parity.
AJ: Main concern: interface stability. How do we version the internal APIs?
Maria G: Plan: use explicit API version headers and a compatibility shim on the monolith for 6 months. New services expose v1/ v2 routes. Router will rewrite traffic only when the bolt-on test passes.
Samir: Does this require DB schema migrations? Any blocking writes?
Maria G: We avoid a global schema change. For session and kv-cache we’ll introduce a side-store and dual-write pattern: write to monolith store + new store while reads prefer new store after warmup. Dual-read toggle behind feature flag.
Noah T: What about latency — extracting kv-cache to a service could add 1–3ms p99 if not colocated. Have perf budget?
Maria G: Yup — perf SLO: +<5ms p99 for end-to-end in-host requests for the first 3 months. We’ll run perf baselines and auto-fallback to monolith variant if we see degradation.
AJ: How do teams own the split pieces? Who’s the owner for the new session-service?
Maria G: Proposal: infra-runtime team owns the router + adapters; eng-runtime owns session-service and kv-cache internals; eng-ml will keep model-serving contract. We map owners in the RFC doc.
Samir: Rollout strategy? Canary? AB?
Maria G: Canary-by-customer and by-route. Steps: 1) internal traffic only, 2) 1% production traffic, 3) 10% tied to a latency budget, 4) ramp to 100% if metrics OK. We’ll automate rollback with the router gate.
deploy-bot: deploy job #3571 started for canary group alpha — image: session-service:v0.1 — status: running
Noah T: Observability — we need tracing and cost attribution from day 0. Don’t want blind spots.
Maria G: Agreed. Mandatory tracing headers (x-rw-trace) and per-request cost tagging. Telemetry contract: metrics for latency, error, token-cost delta, cpu/gpu utilization. Prometheus + tracing must be in place before step 2.
AJ: Tests? How do we validate correctness of caching semantics during dual-write mode?
Maria G: We'll add a deterministic simulator harness that replays production trace samples against monolith and new stack to check divergence. Also add canary probes that verify KV evictions and session continuity on traffic.
Samir: Any risks for Dedicated/Private customers? Private installs might not want sidecars or extra ports.
Maria G: We'll provide an integrated on-prem packaging option: single binary with adapter mode for private installs. Dedicated hosted customers get the split services. The config layer will expose a single logical endpoint.
AJ: Tech debt paydown — do we tie this to any debt tranche?
Maria G: Yes, propose debt-tranche: 3 sprints of API cleanup + 2 sprints of observability + 4 sprints for extraction. Labelled "strangler-debt-1". We’ll track in the architecture board.
Noah T: Estimated risk events?
Maria G: Top risks: 1) silent divergence between stores, 2) performance regressions, 3) ownership confusion. Mitigations: dual-read asserts, perf gates, and explicit owner on-call + playbook.
AJ: Playbook example?
Maria G: Short playbook:
```
- Detect: alert if service p99 > baseline or error-rate > 0.5%
- Scoped rollback: flip router flag to monolith variant for affected routes
- Investigate: run trace sampling for 10k requests
- Postmortem: 48h RCA + follow-up tickets
```
Samir: Sounds reasonable. Timeline?
Maria G: Week 0–2: adapters + proto APIs. Week 3–6: session-service alpha + tests. Week 7–9: canary + perf verification. Week 10: full ramp if green.
Noah T: Can we get a decision in next architecture sync? I want the owners and budget confirmed.
Maria G: I'll post an RFC update with owners and the debt-tranche epic link. Ping me if you want to join the design review.
AJ: +1 to the plan, want to review dual-write harness.
Samir: I'll take session-service ownership pairing 2 engineers from infra-runtime.
Maria G: Awesome — thanks all. I'll attach the prototype adapter and a small sample traffic capture in the RFC doc.
